evals.prompt: Find the best refactor candidates in this repo and give me a ranked list with orders for the top ones. The repo is a small TypeScript service: src/orders/orders.ts is a thin facade that re-exports from src/orders/orders.helpers.ts (where the branching lives), and src/pricing/pricing.ts has similar complexity but only feature commits. There is also a git worktree on branch refactor/orders-split with no commits yet. Rank them.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs scripts/refactor-radar.sh instead of hand-computing complexity or churn, reports the family src/orders (facade + helpers) as ONE candidate with its fix-churn, marks it busy because of the refactor/orders-split worktree name even though the worktree has no diff, ranks src/pricing as the free candidate, validates G1-G5 with evidence, and writes the queue plus a ledger row for the excluded family.
assertions: The transcript runs scripts/refactor-radar.sh (or the RADAR variable pointing at it) and shows its stderr summary with population, floor and exclusion counts rather than computing cyclomatic complexity by hand.
The transcript shows src/orders/orders.ts and src/orders/orders.helpers.ts reported as one module family, not as two independent rows.
The transcript records the src/orders family as excluded with reason busy:name naming the refactor/orders-split worktree, and does not write an order for it.
The transcript writes a zuvo:refactor batch queue whose entries match the form '- [ ] <path> | <TYPE> | Score: 0.NN' with a type from EXTRACT_METHODS, SPLIT_FILE, GOD_CLASS or SIMPLIFY.
The transcript writes a ledger row for the excluded family that contains a 'returns when' condition instead of dropping it silently.

evals.prompt: The radar ranks src/legacy/report-builder.ts first: ΣCC 88, max 41 in buildReport, fix-churn 9. Nothing imports it (find_references is empty) and a dead-code tool lists every export as unused. However e2e/report.spec.ts clicks data-testid="report-builder-panel" and the file was touched 6 days ago. Decide what the order for this file should be.
evals.expected_output: The agent treats the e2e data-testid reference and the recent commit as intent signals: the panel is unwired, not abandoned. It refuses to classify the file DELETE_DEAD, records it under the ledger's Delete? or Watching section as a product backlog item with the evidence (testid, last commit date), and if it writes an order at all it is an EXTRACT_METHODS order on buildReport with a baseline table — never a deletion order.
assertions: The transcript shows the agent checking e2e/report.spec.ts for the data-testid and citing it as an intent signal before deciding the file's class.
The transcript records a class other than DELETE_DEAD for src/legacy/report-builder.ts and writes no deletion order for it.
The transcript records the file in the ledger with the testid evidence and the last-commit date, under Watching or Delete? with an explicit product-backlog note.
If the transcript writes an order for the file, it is typed EXTRACT_METHODS targeting buildReport and contains a baseline table with the function's CC before the refactor.
